name: Flared jeans

card.summary: Flared jeans widen below the knee, balancing thicker thighs and hips and lengthening the leg line when worn with the right shoe.

quick.overview:
Flared jeans are fitted through the thigh and flare out from the knee or calf. People wear them to balance the proportions of the lower body, and the wide hem over a shoe can make the leg line look longer.

The cut has cycled in and out of fashion since the 1960s. Forum commenters have praised styles that fit closely through the hips then widen at the leg.
quick.how: They are worn as everyday denim, often with boots or platform or heeled shoes that keep the hem off the ground. Fit through the thigh and seat is the part commenters emphasise.
quick.risks: No health risks are documented. Very wide hems can drag on the ground, which is why older styles were paired with platform heels.

lead: Flared jeans, also called bell-bottoms or, in narrower form, bootcut, are denim trousers that widen from the knee downward. As a style choice they are used to give the lower body a balanced silhouette.[1]

Bell-shaped trouser legs began with sailors in the early 19th century and were part of Royal Navy uniform until 1977. The style spread through 1960s London and North America, and Levi's introduced its 646 Bell Bottom in 1969.[1] The cut was a symbol of the 1970s, faded by 1979, returned in narrower bootcut form in the 1990s and 2000s, and came back in wide-leg form around 2022 and 2023.[1]

Posters in T Nation threads have described flared denim fitted around the hips and wider in the leg as a favourite cut for athletic bodies.[2] No studies examine how the cut changes perceived proportions.

chain: Fitted thigh and seat, flare from the knee
Wider hem balances hips and thighs
Leg line looks longer when worn with a heeled shoe
angle.text: The flare offsets the width of the upper body or thighs and lengthens the leg line. Style commenters say fit through the hips matters.

paras: Naval and carpenters' flared trousers pre-date the fashion; the 1960s brought flares in denim, often with Cuban heels or boots, and the 1970s brought wider loon and elephant bell versions worn with platform shoes.[1] Bootcut dominated for about a decade until skinny jeans took over around 2006.[1]

On T Nation, one poster named jeans that fit through the seat and flare below as a favourite style, and another liked wide-leg pants fitting around the hips and wider in the leg for athletic builds.[2][3]
